audit_meta.notes: Docker Desktop was deliberately NOT started and no images were pulled/built during this audit. C: had only 3.73 GiB free at audit time and already hosts a 26.6 GiB Docker WSL virtual disk; pulling or building the AURA stack's images risked exhausting the system drive, which the audit's own safety rules prohibit. Sections needing a live container runtime are therefore CALCULATED/ESTIMATED from configuration plus a REFERENCE benchmark (Phase A4) rather than freshly measured.

cpu.virtualization_caveat: WMI reports VirtualizationFirmwareEnabled=False, but Hyper-V is demonstrably active (WSL2/Docker Desktop require it, and systeminfo confirms 'A hypervisor has been detected'). This is a known WMI artifact once a hypervisor already owns VT-x, not evidence that virtualization is actually disabled.

sequential_io_benchmark_e_drive.method: 256 MiB random-data file written then read via .NET File.WriteAllBytes/ReadAllBytes, deleted immediately after
sequential_io_benchmark_e_drive.read_caveat: The 1333 MB/s read figure is an OS page-cache artifact — the file was read back immediately after being written and was still cached in RAM, not served from the physical HDD. True cold sequential read speed is UNVERIFIED; ESTIMATED 80-150 MB/s typical for this drive's class (5400 RPM 2.5in SATA laptop HDD).

storage.docker_disk_relocation_note: Docker Desktop's disk image location defaults to C: (already 1.6% free). Relocating it to E: (79.4% free) via Docker Desktop Settings > Resources > Advanced is the smallest practical change to unblock any local Docker use.

network.link_speed_caveat: 81 Mbps is far below the AX200 adapter's Wi-Fi 6 potential (600+ Mbps), indicating a constrained access-point link rather than an adapter limitation. Not benchmarked further (throughput/latency/packet-loss) — this is out of scope for local AURA capacity since container-to-container and host-to-container traffic never crosses the Wi-Fi link.

aura_service_inventory.cpu_oversubscription_vs_logical_threads: 16.95 vCPU requested against 12 logical threads on this machine (+41%). Docker CPU limits are soft caps, not reservations, so this manifests as contention under simultaneous full load rather than a hard failure.

This means the Quadro T1000 GPU is architecturally unused by the shipped backend image as configured; using it would require deviating from the pinned lockfile, which is out of this audit's scope (architecture must be preserved).

ai_model_config.documented_target_deployment_profile: deploy/.env.example comments describe the reference deployment as an '8 cores, no NVIDIA' CPU-only VPS, with sandbox workspace defaults assuming a 'documented 24 GB host'. This laptop (6 physical/12 logical threads, 31.8 GB RAM) is in a broadly comparable class on RAM but has fewer physical cores than the VPS's 8 vCPU.

reference_inference_benchmark.evidence: REFERENCE — measured in Phase A4 (docs/reports/phase-a4-load-test.md), on a DIFFERENT machine (a disposable 4-core/15 GB Linux sandbox), NOT this laptop. Included because it uses the identical model and Ollama config this audit's local stack would use, and is the only real measured CPU-inference data available without running a live benchmark here.
reference_inference_benchmark.environment: 4-core / 15 GB Linux container, real Postgres/Qdrant/Redis/Ollama (not in-memory adapters), model qwen2.5:3b-instruct-q4_K_M, OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL=1, AURA_PROVIDER_LOCAL_MAX_CONCURRENCY=1
reference_inference_benchmark.conclusion: Throughput is flat from 1 to 8 concurrent requests — OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL=1 is the confirmed binding constraint, not CPU headroom. This is a configuration ceiling, not a hardware one, and would reproduce on this laptop's hardware as well regardless of its extra cores/RAM versus the A4 sandbox.
reference_inference_benchmark.extrapolation_to_this_machine: CALCULATED — this laptop has more physical cores (6c/12t vs 4c) and over 2x the RAM (31.8 GB vs 15 GB) of the A4 sandbox, so per-turn latency would plausibly be similar-to-modestly-better (CPU-bound GGUF token generation for a 3B model scales sublinearly with cores past ~4-6 due to memory-bandwidth limits), but the single-request concurrency ceiling would reproduce identically since it is a semaphore (OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL=1), not a hardware limit.

safety_decisions.docker_daemon_not_started: C: had 3.73 GiB free; starting Docker Desktop is comparatively low-risk, but pulling/building the stack's images was avoided to prevent filling the drive.
safety_decisions.no_images_pulled_or_built: Would have consumed multiple GB on an already-critical C: drive, or required first relocating Docker's disk image — a configuration change beyond a read-only audit's scope to make unilaterally.
safety_decisions.no_ollama_model_downloaded: Same C:/disk-space reasoning; also, Ollama itself is not installed natively on this machine.
safety_decisions.secrets_not_present: deploy/secrets/ does not exist locally (only deploy/.env* files) — bootstrap-secrets.sh has not been run, so the prod compose cannot start as-is without first generating secrets.
safety_decisions.local_env_file_note: deploy/.env (not committed) is pre-populated with the production VPS's own AURA_DOMAIN (169.58.188.43.nip.io) and AURA_SANDBOX_ENABLED=true — it reads as a working copy of the production environment file rather than a local-only configuration, and was not modified or used to start anything during this audit.
